title: How to Prepare a Conversion Rate Audit Before Hiring
h1: How to prepare a conversion rate audit before hiring
description: Prepare a conversion rate audit: goals, key pages, data to share, what an audit should include, how to prioritize fixes and what to ask a specialist.
intro: A conversion rate audit looks at why visitors to your website do not take the action you want, such as buying, booking or signing up. A good audit points to specific changes in order of likely impact. A poor one is a long list of generic tips. The difference often comes from preparation. This article explains what to gather and decide before you hire a conversion specialist.

faq.a: It is the share of visitors who complete a chosen action, such as a purchase or a form submission.

faq.q: Do I need a lot of traffic first?
faq.a: Some traffic helps, because very small numbers make results unreliable. An expert review can still find obvious problems on a low-traffic site.

faq.q: What does an audit usually include?
faq.a: A review of key pages, the visitor journey, mobile experience, page speed, messaging, trust signals and tracking, with prioritized recommendations.

faq.q: Will the specialist make the changes?
faq.a: Not always. Many audits deliver recommendations only. Ask whether implementation is included or priced separately.

faq.q: How long before I see results?
faq.a: It depends on traffic and what you change. Expect to test and measure over weeks, not days.
